article.title: Venice's Gyllenhaal says women directors face 'systemic' barriers
article.summary: VENICE: Venice Film Festival jury president Maggie Gyllenhaal said on Wednesday that cinema was inherently political and that women continue to face systemic obstacles in the film industry, questioning who gets to decide which stories matter.Speaking on the festival’s opening day, Gyllenhaal said films foster empathy at a time of global turmoil and argued that female filmmakers often struggle to secure financing because the stories they want to tell are not considered important.“Could it be possible that the things that women, having had a different experience of being alive in the world want to make movies about are not always deemed high art? … Who decides what’s good?” she said when asked about the scarcity of women directors in Venice.“There’s a systemic problem,” she added.Only two of the 21 films in the main programme at this year’s festival, which runs from September 2-12, are directed or co-directed by women.Venice Film Festival turns to politics as Hollywood retreatsFestiva...

article.title: Venice film shows Murdoch shaking up hidebound Britain
article.summary: ROME: British director Danny Boyle’s new movie “Ink”, unveiled on Wednesday, examines how Rupert Murdoch’s assault on Britain’s media establishment was first embraced as a breath of fresh air before turning into a much darker story.“Ink” opens the 83rd Venice Film Festival, giving Boyle a high-profile launch for a project he joked many people initially thought was about tattoos rather than the newspaper industry.The film, adapted from James Graham’s stage play, charts Murdoch’s acquisition of “The Sun” in 1969 and the transformation of Britain’s once-staid newspaper industry.“It was important to us that the audience felt complicit,” Boyle told reporters. “We were all complicit in this journey to begin with. Scarcity of women directors at Venice due to 'systemic issue' says Gyllenhaal
article.summary:
(ANSA) - ROME, SEP 2 - The under-representation of female directors in Venice and at other international film festivals is due to a "systemic issue", jury chair Maggie Gyllenhaal told a press conference before the 83rd edition of the world's oldest film fest Wednesday, noting that only two women are up for the Golden Lion this year compared to six last year.
"I think it's finally become clear that men make better films than women," Gyllenhaal initially responded with a quip that got the audience laughing when asked about the lack of female directorial talent on show.
"I'll answer seriously, there's a systemic problem," Gyllenhaal added during the press conference with festival director Alberto Barbera and the chairs of this year's other juries.
"I think it's much more difficult for women than men to get funding for their films. Furthermore, it's possible that the themes women tackle, having had a different life experience, aren't always considered high-level art.

article.title: US led by incompetents, with midterms things will return to normal-Clooney in Venice
article.summary:
(ANSA) - ROME, SEP 2 - The United States is currently led by incompetents and things will return to normal after Democrats sweep the midterm elections in November, George Clooney said on his arrival at the Venice Film Festival Wednesday where he is picking up a career achievement Golden Lion Wednesday night.
"It's not easy to live in a country led by the least capable people, said the Hollywood heart throb, 65, on the Lido ahead of the opening night of the 83rd Venice International Film Festival, speaking about his native land without ever mentioning President Donald Trump.
"The midterm elections are in November, which will certainly be a time to take stock, and if all goes well, we'll return to a more normal situation." (ANSA).Read article...

article.title: Jane Fonda and Gisèle Pelicot among winners of 2026 DVF Awards in Venice
article.summary:
(ANSA) - ROME, SEP 1 - Jane Fonda and Gisèlle Pelicot are among the recipients of the 17th Diane von Furstenberg awards at this year's Venice Film Festival.
Actress and activist Fonda; Barbados Prime Minister Mia Amor Mottley; photojournalist Lynsey Addario; Food4Education Founder and CEO Wawira Njiru; and multiple rape survivor, author and activist Pelicot are the winners of the "DVF Awards," promoted by 79-year-old fashion designer von Furstenberg to recognize women global leaders, activists, artists, and changemakers of extraordinary talent.
The awards ceremony will be held in Venice on September 3.
Over the years, the DVF Awards have given voice and visibility to women from more than thirty countries, supporting their work through financial contributions to promote initiatives in a variety of fields, from the fight against climate change and human trafficking, to the promotion of gender equality and the prevention of violence against women.

article.title: Venice Film Festival turns to politics as Hollywood retreats
article.summary: VENICE: Hollywood is struggling with an industry crisis and has largely withdrawn from this year’s Venice Film Festival, making way for a programme steeped in global politics and social upheaval, the event’s director said on Tuesday.Festival director Alberto Barbera said the gritty line-up reflected filmmakers’ growing engagement with contemporary events, ranging from the conflict in Gaza and Russia’s invasion of Ukraine to the rise of billionaires and immigration enforcement in the United States.The world’s oldest film festival, which begins on Wednesday and runs until September 12, traditionally marks the start of the awards season, but many of the studio-backed Oscar contenders that once crowded its schedule are absent, just as they were from Cannes in May.“The problem is Hollywood. They face a huge crisis,” Barbera told Reuters. “They’re producing fewer films, more costly. Some of them work very well and some of them are, on the contrary, a commercial disaster. article.title: ‘He was always a bit of a groundbreaker’: David Bowie enters a new dimension in ‘extended reality’ documentary
article.summary: Hundreds of unseen images of the star feature at the Venice film festival, alongside virtual worlds exploring wildfires, wolves and the birth of starsDavid Bowie shares the bill with starmen, firefighters and Walt Disney wolves at the 10th anniversary edition of Venice Immersive, the film festival’s pioneering showcase for new forms of storytelling. David Bowie: Unseen Unheard – a 3D documentary featuring hundreds of previously unseen images – is among 69 XR (extended reality) pieces playing at the event’s regular base on Lazzaretto Vecchio, a repurposed small island off the Venice Lido.Venice Immersive’s 10th birthday marks a milestone for an event which aims to provide a bridge between emergent technology and traditional narrative cinema.
